subject: Culture
title: Naming and Lineage
description: A 60-second lesson on Naming and Lineage.

hook.text: Icelandic phone books are sorted by first name because surnames are just your father's name plus 'son' or 'dóttir.'

buildup.text: Patronymic systems tie your identity to your father's line. Matronymic ones trace the mother. Some cultures use both.

discovery.text: Surnames became mandatory in Europe only around the 1400s—tax collectors needed them to track people.

twist.text: In many African traditions your name tells the day you were born, the season, or the event marking your arrival.

climax.text: Changing your family name after immigration is a quiet act of cultural erasure that haunts later generations.

punchline.text: Your name is your family's first gift and story.

quiz.question: Why did surnames become mandatory in Europe?
